newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP closure could cost up to 12,000 jobs - union.
newsitem.headline: BHP closure could cost up to 12,000 jobs - union.

text.p: The downstream effects of the phase-out of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) Newcastle steelworks could cause the loss of up to 12,000 jobs Australia-wide, Mark Stoker, acting assistant secretary of the Australian Workers Union (AWU) at Newcastle, said on Tuesday.
BHP, in announcing the phase-out earlier on Tuesday, said that 2,500 jobs would be directly lost because of the closure but the union believed the direct loss would be closer to 3,000 jobs, he said.
"The downstream effects could be up to 12,000," he said.
After the job cuts, only 400 to 500 people would be left working for BHP Steel at Newcastle, he said.
A union delegates meeting had been called for Tuesday afternoon which would be attended by Bob Carr, the Labor premier of New South Wales, he said.
A mass meeting of union members would be held on Friday, he said.
"We're expecting that there will be a fair bit of emotion at the mass meeting," Stoker said.
Asked for his assessment of whether a strike would be called on Friday, Stoker said this would be a consideration.
Further questions on strike matters should be directed to Mauri Rudd, Newcastle secretary of the AWU, he said.
Reuters earlier on Tuesday asked Rudd if possible strike action would attempt to block BHP exports.
"Yeah, we'll try and do all that," Rudd said.
